hero.headline: St. Lucie County firefighter firings disputed as police report contradicts hazing investigation
hero.body:
St. Lucie County Fire Chief Jeff Lee terminated three senior firefighters and suspended two others following an outside investigation into an alleged hazing incident reported to the department in March 2026. An investigative summary prepared by an outside law firm concluded that senior personnel had modified a bug zapper to shock three apprentice firefighters while on duty in 2024. The investigation was launched after six videos surfaced that the report says appeared to show hazing, workplace violence or other misconduct.

A Fort Pierce Police report obtained by WPTV reaches a very different conclusion. A Fort Pierce police officer wrote that after interviewing the three firefighters who were shocked, he found there was no criminal matter behind the alleged hazing and that the videos showed coworkers entertaining each other. The report states the acts were done by their own will, and that every person originally listed as a victim said they are not victims and did not want to continue the investigation.

Retired Fire Captain Mike Jenkins, who served more than 30 years with the department, watched the videos and said he does not believe they show hazing. Jenkins was one of several people who spoke at last week's fire board meeting, calling the incident a harmless, consensual prank and warning the firings could have broader consequences. "This is not just going to affect this place. This is going to be used all over the country," Jenkins said. "This was not violence. I mean, these kids wanted to do this." The St Lucie County Chapter of the Professional Fire Fighters & Paramedics Union also disputes the investigation, calling it biased and saying it reached a predetermined conclusion. Union President Ryan Sapp wrote that the investigation was not conducted in an impartial or unbiased manner and noted that the law firm that conducted the investigation is now representing the Fire District at arbitration.

Chief Lee pointed to four prior harassment complaints involving Station 1, including one that specifically named the three firefighters who were ultimately terminated. Those complaints prompted Lee to retain independent outside counsel, which launched a separate investigation into Station 1 in June 2025. That investigation interviewed 30 employees over two days, with interviewees describing the station as an environment characterized by intense peer pressure, social exclusion, and inappropriate banter. The reassignment of the three firefighters in August 2025 prompted them and others to file 12 complaints against Lee and other administrators with three separate state agencies. All 12 complaints have been dismissed. The union is now demanding arbitration on behalf of the terminated and suspended firefighters.

cards.headline: Child killed, another injured in bicycle crash with FedEx truck on East Midway Road in Fort Pierce
cards.body:
A child died and another was hospitalized after a bicycle collided with a FedEx truck Monday afternoon in Fort Pierce, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The crash happened around 3:07 p.m. in the 600 block of East Midway Road. Two juveniles were riding a bicycle when it collided with the FedEx truck. One child was pronounced dead at the scene, while the second child was transported to a hospital in stable condition. Officials have not released the identities or ages of the children involved in the crash.

Neighbors who live near the crash site told WPTV that the area is commonly used by people riding bicycles. Megan Sharma, a resident who lives close to where the incident occurred, described the tragedy as horrible. She said children are frequently seen riding up and down the sidewalk on both sides of the road. Sharma expressed sorrow over the fatal outcome, calling it really tragic that a child died in the collision.

Sharma noted this was not the first deadly incident on East Midway Road. She recalled that several years ago in 2020, a young adult on a motorcycle was struck by a car along the same stretch of road. Given the history of crashes in the area, Sharma urged people to exercise extreme caution. She advised looking both ways before crossing the street and being wary of other vehicles, describing East Midway Road as a very dangerous highway.

The Florida Highway Patrol is investigating the incident. No additional details about what led up to the collision have been released at this time. Authorities have not provided information about whether any charges will be filed or what factors may have contributed to the crash between the bicycle and the FedEx truck.

cards.headline: Parents file wrongful death lawsuit after 6-year-old dies in go-kart crash at Port St. Lucie Urban Air park
cards.teaser: The family of Emma Riddle claims Urban Air Trampoline and Adventure Park in Port St. Lucie ignored safety rules and manufacturer guidelines before the fatal December 2025 crash.
cards.body:
A wrongful death lawsuit was filed Monday against Urban Air Trampoline and Adventure Park in Port St. Lucie after 6-year-old Emma Riddle died in a go-kart crash at the facility in December 2025. The child's parents allege that Urban Air created dangerous conditions that contributed to Emma's death. Emma visited the adventure park with her mother and sister, where they rode electric go-karts. The child was seated with her mom in a double-seat go-kart while her older sister was in a single-rider go-kart. According to the family's attorney, Morgan & Morgan injury law firm, the complaint outlines multiple alleged safety protocols ignored that allegedly led Emma's go-kart to accelerate to a high speed and crash into the track wall. Emma suffered severe injuries and was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where she later died.

The lawsuit alleges the adventure park ignored safety rules and manufacturer guidelines. At 50 inches, Emma was nearly a foot shorter and twelve years younger than the manufacturer's minimum stated recommendations for operating a double-seat go-kart, and yet she was permitted to ride. Earlier this year, the Florida Department of Agriculture reached a $300,000 settlement agreement with Urban Air Adventure Park following an investigation into the fatal incident. Morgan & Morgan founder John Morgan said in a statement that Urban Air has a duty to protect every child that walks through their doors, and the firm alleges they failed Emma.

cards.headline: Federal judge weighs Florida's promise that Alligator Alcatraz detention facility won't reopen
cards.body:
A federal judge in Florida heard arguments Monday on whether the state's closure of the controversial Alligator Alcatraz immigration detention facility is permanent, as aerial photos filed in court show the remote Everglades airstrip now sits empty. The images, captured over the weekend and filed with sworn declarations by Florida Division of Emergency Management officials, show what was once a sprawling complex of trailers, tents, generators, and lights is now just an airstrip with a few trucks scattered around.

Immigration attorneys and former detainees have sued the state and federal government, arguing civil rights violations occurred due to inadequate attorney-client access at the facility. The state and federal government contend the case is now moot because the facility is closed. Nicholas Meros, an attorney representing Florida, told the judge there is no reasonable likelihood the facility will reopen. However, ACLU attorney Amy Godshall challenged those assurances, noting that the state set up the facility in 10 days when it first opened, still controls the land, and has not returned it to Miami-Dade County. The Miami-Dade Mayor's Office confirmed Monday afternoon it has not gotten the land back, which the state took using emergency powers.

The closure came after the state spent more than $1 billion on the facility and has not been reimbursed by the federal government. Governor Ron DeSantis announced in October that FEMA had approved a $608 million grant for Alligator Alcatraz, but court filings in a separate federal lawsuit revealed FEMA had not disbursed the funding because of ongoing litigation. A DHS spokesperson said the agency reviews reimbursement requests for grant funding to ensure costs are allowable and validated expenses eligible for reimbursement prior to releasing funding, but FEMA has not answered direct questions about whether it would reimburse the Florida Division of Emergency Management.

Meros denied in court Monday that the facility closed for financial reasons or to avoid discovery in court. He said he could not speak for future administrations but stated the state has no intention to reopen it. Meanwhile, an ICE spokesperson told WPTV on Monday that the agency is pursuing all available options to expand bedspace capacity, including partnering with states, local governments, and private sector partners to house detainees at existing facilities. The state initially said in June it was relocating detainees for hurricane season, though DeSantis also made public statements that Alligator Alcatraz had served its intended purpose of adding bed space for immigration detainees.

cards.headline: Stuart woman arrested after deputies rescue 80 cats from home in worst hoarding case Martin County sheriff has seen
cards.body:
Martin County deputies rescued dozens of cats Monday from a Stuart home that Sheriff John Budensiek described as the worst animal hoarding case he has seen in the county. The Martin County Sheriff's Office, Animal Control and Martin County Fire Rescue responded to a home in the 11500 block of Southwest Meadowlark Circle after an investigation into reports that a U.S. Postal Service employee had been collecting feral cats along her mail route. Budensiek identified the homeowner as 77-year-old Gail Giustino and said investigators believe she was not stealing pets but was gathering feral cats and bringing them home.

Authorities obtained a search warrant after Giustino allegedly refused to allow Animal Control officers inside the home during multiple attempts over the past week. When deputies entered the house Monday, they found what the sheriff described as horrific living conditions. The home had no working air conditioning, little to no ventilation and, in some areas, up to a foot of animal feces covering the floor. Budensiek said the odor was overwhelming, and Martin County Fire Rescue's Hazardous Materials Team had to ventilate the home before rescuers could safely enter. Giustino told deputies she believed there were at least 70 cats inside the home, all kept in cages. Authorities believe there could ultimately be 70 to 80 animals or more, including several dogs, though an exact count had not been completed Monday evening.

The rescued animals are being taken to the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast, which is expected to rely on foster families and volunteers to help care for them. Authorities said they are still evaluating the animals' medical conditions. Budensiek said Giustino was arrested on two misdemeanor animal cruelty related charges, though investigators said they could have pursued significantly more charges. The sheriff explained that the criminal charges were filed primarily to obtain the search warrant, remove the animals from the home and prevent Giustino from acquiring additional animals while she seeks help through the mental health court system.

Officials said Animal Control had previously cited Giustino dozens of times for animal related violations about 10 years ago, but they believe she gradually returned to hoarding animals after complying with earlier code enforcement requirements. Budensiek said authorities believe Giustino thinks she is doing the right thing but is doing it the wrong way. "If we believe she was truly an animal abuser, we would try to bury her under the jail," Budensiek said. "We truly believe that Gail thinks she's doing the right thing, but she's doing it the wrong way."

cards.headline: St. Lucie County firefighters' union disputes hazing investigation, demands arbitration after terminations
cards.teaser: The union representing St. Lucie County Fire District firefighters is challenging the termination of three firefighters and suspension of two others, calling the investigation biased and the disciplinary actions unjust.
cards.body:
Professional Firefighters and Paramedics of St. Lucie County, IAFF Local 1377, said the St. Lucie County Fire District wrongly terminated and suspended the five members for their involvement in incidents that occurred in March and September 2024. Local 1377 President Ryan Sapp stated in a letter obtained by WPTV that these incidents did not involve any hazing. Sapp pointed to the Fort Pierce Police Department's report, which he said described the situation, in part, as "found coworkers entertaining each other." The union's position is that all five were wrongly found to be in violation of fire district policies and disciplined without just cause. Sapp also noted that members involved in the incidents were treated differently during the investigative and disciplinary processes, with some receiving no discipline at all.

The union raised concerns about the outside law firm the fire district hired to conduct its investigation, Allen, Norton & Blue. Local 1377 and its legal counsel said the investigation was not conducted in an impartial or unbiased manner. Sapp stated in the letter that the nature of the questions asked, as well as the way in which they were asked or not asked, reflects a predetermined conclusion rather than an objective fact-finding process. Sapp noted that the same firm that conducted the investigation has since been hired by the fire district to represent it at arbitration. Local 1377 has demanded arbitration for all five members and remains willing to negotiate a reasonable resolution that would avoid the significant costs of arbitration and save both the taxpayers and the Local a substantial amount of money. Sapp said Fire Chief Jeff Lee has not offered any concessions or proposed resolutions.

cards.headline: Florida's back-to-school tax-free holiday runs through Aug. 20
cards.teaser: Families across the Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast are heading to stores to take advantage of the savings during Florida's back-to-school tax-free holiday.
cards.body:
Families across the Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast are shopping during Florida's tax-free holiday to save on back-to-school supplies. Katrina Stoneking was shopping at Office Depot in Boynton Beach for her soon-to-be 5th grader when she said she typically spends around $200 or more each year on school supplies. She said she's hoping to save probably $50 to $60 during the holiday. WPTV priced a random school supply list for a fourth grader in Palm Beach County and the items rang up to about $263.52, which saves $18.45 in taxes alone during the holiday. Tameica Petgrave, the general manager of the Boynton Beach Office Depot, said 3-ring paper is the item parents have been asking about most. She said the tax discount is applied automatically at checkout on qualifying items.

Clothing and accessories priced under $100 each are tax free, including shirts, pants, backpacks, wallets, belts, and graduation caps and gowns. General school supplies priced under $50 each are also exempt, including pens, pencils, and lunch boxes. Flashcards and educational toys priced under $30 each qualify, and electronics like calculators, printers, laptops, and tablets all qualify as long as each item is under $1,500 and purchased for personal use only. Business purchases do not qualify. Items ordered online during the holiday period qualify for the exemption, even if they are delivered after Aug. 20. The official first day of school in the Palm Beaches and the Treasure Coast is Aug. 10, and the tax-free holiday runs through Aug. 20.

cards.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
cards.teaser: Murray Middle School demolition is underway in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton.
cards.body:
Murray Middle School demolition is underway in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project includes reconstruction of buildings destroyed in the tornadoes, along with a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a full overhaul of the parking lot. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized.

 The project is being funded by local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay. Students who were displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete.

 Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, said Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab. With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine, the district was able to add these on.

 The school district said parents can be assured their students will be safe during construction. Barriers have already been placed around the work zone to keep students out. The district hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027.

cards.headline: Tuition-free tech charter school to open in Fort Pierce next month with 460 students
cards.teaser: SouthTech Treasure Coast will open in Fort Pierce in August, bringing tuition-free career and technical education to middle and high school students on the Treasure Coast. The St.
cards.body:
SouthTech Treasure Coast will open in Fort Pierce in August, bringing tuition-free career and technical education to middle and high school students on the Treasure Coast. The St. Lucie County School Board approved the charter application in April. School leaders selected the Treasure Coast location because of the area's growing demand for skilled workers.

 The Fort Pierce campus will serve students in grades 6 through 12, with plans to enroll about 460 students in its first year. Students will choose from career academies including medical science, culinary arts, cosmetology, agriculture technology, and other programs similar to those offered at the existing Boynton Beach campus. The school allows students to earn adult level industry certifications while completing traditional coursework, helping them build real-world skills and prepare for high-demand careers before they graduate.

 Carla Lovett, Executive Director of SouthTech Schools, said all students are working on their academics while also participating in one of the career academies where they can earn adult level industry certifications while still in high school. Nicole Handy, Director of Expansion of SouthTech Schools, said the school is targeting high paying careers that are growing and expanding in the Fort Pierce area.

 Meghan Hess Shamdasani, Career and Technical Education Program Coordinator, said it's better to learn something for free when you're a kid than to pay for it in college and learn. School leaders say the goal is to give students a head start on their careers by helping them graduate with valuable skills and certifications before entering the workforce or continuing their education.

 SouthTech Treasure Coast will host a grand opening celebration on Saturday, July 25, from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m., giving families and community members a chance to tour the new campus and learn more about the programs being offered. The school is located at 2810 S. US Highway 1 in Fort Pierce. The new campus is based on a model already operating at SouthTech Academy in Boynton Beach, which has spent years combining traditional academics with hands-on career training.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County residents adjust diets as E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks spread
cards.teaser: Health officials confirmed five local cases of cyclospora since May, including two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County, prompting residents to change what they eat and avoid.
cards.body:
Concerns over contaminated produce linked to E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks are prompting South Florida residents to reconsider their food choices, with some avoiding leafy greens entirely. The outbreaks have affected thousands nationwide and include lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials have confirmed local cases stretching from the Palm Beaches to the Treasure Coast, including two cases in St. Lucie County.

 The Florida Department of Health reported five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May. Two cases were reported in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County, and one in Martin County. The contamination concerns have led families across the region to change their eating habits at restaurants, grocery stores, and fast-food chains.

 Dakota and Brynlee Rhodes, who were visiting Delray Beach with their mother Jenny, said they are trying to stay away from lettuce and stuff like that. Other families are similarly steering clear of leafy greens altogether as reports of contaminated produce continue to spread across the country. The widespread nature of the outbreaks has left many consumers uncertain about which products are safe to purchase and consume.

 Samantha Barone, a dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, offered guidance for consumers looking to maintain healthy diets while avoiding potentially contaminated produce. Barone recommends sticking to melon and things that have a harder skin that you can peel. She advises consumers to focus on produce with protective outer layers and to wash all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them.

 For those seeking alternatives to leafy greens, Barone suggests that beans and nuts are safe options that still provide fiber and protein. She specifically recommends cleaning produce using a mixture of one part distilled white vinegar to three parts water. The outbreaks have highlighted the importance of proper food handling and preparation practices for consumers across South Florida.
