cards.headline: St. Lucie County residents adjust diets as E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks spread
cards.teaser: Health officials confirmed five local cases of cyclospora since May, including two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County, prompting residents to change what they eat and avoid.
cards.body:
Concerns over contaminated produce linked to E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks are prompting South Florida residents to reconsider their food choices, with some avoiding leafy greens entirely. The outbreaks have affected thousands nationwide and include lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials have confirmed local cases stretching from the Palm Beaches to the Treasure Coast, including two cases in St. Lucie County.

 The Florida Department of Health reported five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May. Two cases were reported in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County, and one in Martin County. The contamination concerns have led families across the region to change their eating habits at restaurants, grocery stores, and fast-food chains.

 Dakota and Brynlee Rhodes, who were visiting Delray Beach with their mother Jenny, said they are trying to stay away from lettuce and stuff like that. Other families are similarly steering clear of leafy greens altogether as reports of contaminated produce continue to spread across the country. The widespread nature of the outbreaks has left many consumers uncertain about which products are safe to purchase and consume.

 Samantha Barone, a dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, offered guidance for consumers looking to maintain healthy diets while avoiding potentially contaminated produce. Barone recommends sticking to melon and things that have a harder skin that you can peel. She advises consumers to focus on produce with protective outer layers and to wash all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them.

 For those seeking alternatives to leafy greens, Barone suggests that beans and nuts are safe options that still provide fiber and protein. She specifically recommends cleaning produce using a mixture of one part distilled white vinegar to three parts water. The outbreaks have highlighted the importance of proper food handling and preparation practices for consumers across South Florida.

cards.headline: E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks hit Treasure Coast, residents avoid lettuce and berries
cards.teaser: Two confirmed cases of cyclospora infections occurred in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County since May, part of nationwide E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks linked to contamin
cards.body:
Two confirmed cases of cyclospora infections occurred in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County since May, part of nationwide E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks linked to contaminated lettuce, according to the Florida Department of Health. Palm Beach County reported two additional cases. Thousands across the United States have been affected by the outbreaks, including lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations.

 Residents across South Florida are changing their diets in response to the health threat. Dakota and Brynlee Rhodes, visiting Delray Beach with their mother Jenny, said they are staying away from lettuce. Jenny Rhodes said she misses salads and berries but prefers being careful.

 George Lorenz said he heard about the outbreak and is avoiding contaminated foods while eating pizza in downtown West Palm Beach on Clematis Street with his father Brian. Hendriette Peckens in Boynton Beach bought two big bags of oranges, bread and apples instead of produce and planned to cook Alaskan salmon for dinner.

 Samantha Barone, a dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, said consumers should focus on produce with protective outer layers like melons, bananas and avocados. She said people should stick to melon and things with harder skin that can be peeled, but emphasized the importance of washing them before cutting and peeling. Barone recommended washing all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them and said beans and nuts are safe alternatives that provide fiber and protein.

 She warned against bagged lettuce and recommended buying whole heads of lettuce and peeling away the outer layers. She also advised avoiding berries, especially raspberries, because they are difficult to clean properly. Brian Lorenz said he is not avoiding anything but is washing all food.

 Barone recommended cleaning produce using a one to three part mixture of distilled white vinegar and water, then soaking, massaging and cleaning off produce before cooking vegetables. The outbreaks stem from contaminated produce that can cause severe stomach illness and intense diarrhea. Barone emphasized that the outbreaks are not an excuse to abandon healthy eating, telling people not to say to heck with fruits and vegetables and hit the donuts. She said consumers still want to remain healthy despite the contamination concerns affecting produce typically considered healthier options.

hero.headline: Family files wrongful death lawsuit against Urban Air Adventure Park in Port St. Lucie after 6-year-old dies in go-kart crash
hero.teaser: The parents of Emma Riddle filed a wrongful death lawsuit Monday against Urban Air Trampoline and Adventure Park, alleging the Port St. Lucie business created dangerous conditions that led to their daughter's death in December 2025.
hero.body:
Emma Riddle, 6, was fatally injured at Urban Air Trampoline and Adventure Park in Port St. Lucie in December 2025. A wrongful death lawsuit was filed Monday by the child's parents against the business. Emma visited the adventure park with her mother and sister, where they rode electric go-karts. The child was seated with her mom in a double-seat go-kart while her older sister was in a single-rider go-kart. According to the family's attorney, Morgan & Morgan injury law firm, there were multiple alleged safety protocols ignored that allegedly led Emma's go-kart to accelerate to a high speed and crash into the track wall. Emma suffered severe injuries and was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where she later died.

The child's parents allege that Urban Air created dangerous conditions that contributed to Emma's death. The lawsuit claims the adventure park ignored safety rules and manufacturer guidelines. At 50 inches, Emma was nearly a foot shorter and twelve years younger than the manufacturer's minimum stated recommendations for operating a double-seat go-kart, and yet she was permitted to ride, the lawsuit alleges. Earlier this year, WPTV obtained documents showing the Florida Department of Agriculture reached a $300,000 settlement agreement with Urban Air Adventure Park following an investigation into the fatal incident. Morgan & Morgan founder John Morgan said in a statement that Urban Air has a duty to protect every child that walks through their doors, and the firm alleges they failed Emma.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County firefighters' union disputes hazing investigation, demands arbitration after terminations
cards.teaser: The union representing St. Lucie County Fire District firefighters is challenging the termination of three firefighters and suspension of two others, calling the investigation biased and the disciplinary actions unjust.
cards.body:
Professional Firefighters and Paramedics of St. Lucie County, IAFF Local 1377, said the St. Lucie County Fire District wrongly terminated and suspended the five members for their involvement in incidents that occurred in March and September 2024. Local 1377 President Ryan Sapp stated in a letter obtained by WPTV that these incidents did not involve any hazing. Sapp pointed to the Fort Pierce Police Department's report, which he said described the situation, in part, as "found coworkers entertaining each other." The union's position is that all five were wrongly found to be in violation of fire district policies and disciplined without just cause. Sapp also noted that members involved in the incidents were treated differently during the investigative and disciplinary processes, with some receiving no discipline at all.

The union raised concerns about the outside law firm the fire district hired to conduct its investigation, Allen, Norton & Blue. Local 1377 and its legal counsel said the investigation was not conducted in an impartial or unbiased manner. Sapp stated in the letter that the nature of the questions asked, as well as the way in which they were asked or not asked, reflects a predetermined conclusion rather than an objective fact-finding process. Sapp noted that the same firm that conducted the investigation has since been hired by the fire district to represent it at arbitration. Local 1377 has demanded arbitration for all five members and remains willing to negotiate a reasonable resolution that would avoid the significant costs of arbitration and save both the taxpayers and the Local a substantial amount of money. Sapp said Fire Chief Jeff Lee has not offered any concessions or proposed resolutions.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce police report contradicts St. Lucie County Fire District hazing investigation that led to firefighter firings
cards.teaser: Three St. Lucie County firefighters were fired following an investigation into alleged hazing, but a Fort Pierce police report and community members are questioning whether the punishment fits the case.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County Fire Chief Jeff Lee issued a press release over the weekend announcing the termination of three senior St. Lucie County firefighters following an investigation into an alleged hazing incident that Lee said was reported to the department in March 2026. An investigative summary prepared by an outside law firm hired by the St. Lucie County Fire District concluded that senior personnel had modified a bug zapper to shock three apprentice firefighters while on duty in 2024. The investigation was launched after six videos surfaced that the report says appeared to show hazing, workplace violence or other misconduct. Lee said in his statement that the investigation found the three employees were subjected to hazing by senior personnel and supervisors. Three supervisors were fired, while two other firefighters were suspended.

A Fort Pierce police report obtained by WPTV appears to reach a very different conclusion. A Fort Pierce police officer wrote that after interviewing the three firefighters who were shocked, he found there was no criminal matter behind the alleged hazing and that the videos showed coworkers entertaining each other. The report also states the acts were done by their own will, and that every person originally listed as a victim said they are not victims and did not want to continue the investigation. Retired Fire Captain Mike Jenkins, who served more than 30 years with the department, watched the videos and said he does not believe they show hazing. Chief Lee pointed to four prior harassment complaints involving Station 1, including one that specifically named the three firefighters who were ultimately terminated.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie to Host Low-Cost Rabies and Microchip Drive-Thru Clinic Aug. 22
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie Animal Control will host a Low-Cost Rabies & Microchip Drive-Thru Clinic next month, giving local pet owners an affordable opportunity to vaccinate and microchip the
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie Animal Control will host a Low-Cost Rabies & Microchip Drive-Thru Clinic next month, giving local pet owners an affordable opportunity to vaccinate and microchip their dogs and cats.

The clinic will take place from 8 a.m. to 2 p.m. on Saturday, Aug. 22, in the Animal Control parking lot at 1133 SW South Macedo Blvd. The drive-thru format allows residents to remain in their vehicles throughout the process. Vehicles should enter from SW Lakehurst Drive via Bayshore Boulevard.

The event is open only to Port St. Lucie residents, who must provide proof of residency, such as a driver's license or utility bill.

For $20 per pet, participants will receive:

- A one-year rabies vaccination
- A microchip
- A City of Port St. Lucie pet license

Dogs and cats must be at least 4 months old to participate. Dogs must arrive on a leash, while cats must be transported in secure carriers. Animal Control officials noted that all dogs will be muzzled during their appointment to ensure staff safety.

The clinic is limited to 200 pets, and walk-up appointments will not be accepted. Pet owners are required to register in advance.

**Preregistration is required.** You can [preregister for the clinic here](https://forms.cityofpsl.com/AnimalLicensing/RabiesMicrochip/RabiesMicrochipForm).

The event is being held in partnership with Caring Fields Feline Sanctuary, Operation SOS, and the Humane Society of St. Lucie County.

cards.headline: Second arrest made in fatal shooting of Fort Pierce art teacher Andre Leonard Barnes
cards.teaser: Dale A. Mincey, 41, Barnes' nephew, was formally charged with first-degree murder Saturday in connection with the July 7 shooting on the 2700 block of Essex Drive.
cards.body:
The fatal shooting happened July 7 at a residence on the 2700 block of Essex Drive. Deputies responded to the home at around 3:30 p.m. after receiving reports of a person with a gunshot wound. When deputies arrived, they learned a man had shot another man with a rifle.

 Barnes was taken to a local hospital, where he died. Dale A. Mincey, 41, Barnes' nephew, was formally charged with first-degree murder Saturday in connection with Barnes' death.

 Mincey remains in custody at the St. Lucie County Jail and is being held without bond. During questioning, Mincey told detectives he could not recall what happened the day of the shooting and that he didn't have any issues with Barnes and did not know how Barnes died, an arrest affidavit said. However, he admitted to owning two firearms.

 Karen Moye, the victim's sister and mother of the suspect, was also at the home when the shooting occurred. She heard a loud bang while she was in the bathroom and came out to find Mincey and called police, an arrest affidavit said. Moye, who lived in the home with Mincey and Barnes, told detectives immediately after the shooting that the pair did not have a good relationship and that Mincey told her he was expressing fear in the days leading up to the shooting.

 Sheriff Richard Del Toro said Moye knowingly provided false information to investigators and withheld pertinent information related to this homicide investigation. She has been charged with false report to law enforcement and the commission of a capital felony. Barnes worked as an art teacher for the St. Lucie County School District since 2017, serving at West Gate K-8 and Samuel S. Gaines Academy.

cards.headline: Some Villa Del Sol residents return home nearly 2 years after structural damage forced evacuation
cards.teaser: Villa Del Sol residents in St. Lucie County told WPTV they are able to return home after nearly two years of being displaced from their condos following structural damage found in August 2024.
cards.body:
Residents told WPTV they were notified last month they could return to their condos, after an inspection in August 2024 found structural damage in buildings 3, 4, and 5, which were deemed unsafe. Katie Johnson was the first to share to WPTV that residents had been told they could come back. WPTV received emails sent to residents from the Board of Directors telling them they could return.

 WPTV also obtained a letter from engineers sent to St. Lucie County's Building Department requesting they lift occupancy restrictions following their special inspection. Katie Johnson described the work still underway at the property, saying they're still moving the dirt back under the buildings.

 Robert Segedin took WPTV inside his family's home, excited to return but thinking about those who cannot. Eric Johnson is among those not coming back. He was one of the first residents WPTV met at Villa Del Sol and is now living in Georgia.

 Eric Johnson said the financial toll has been severe, explaining the family had to drain out all their savings accounts and all their 401ks just trying to make ends meet while this was going on. He is filing for bankruptcy and filing his condo for foreclosure. Katie Johnson said she is thinking of neighbors like Eric Johnson who cannot return, saying she feels so bad that some were hit harder than others with the situation.

hero.headline: Fellsmere animal sanctuary rebuilds with steel after March fire killed 11 cats
hero.body:
For the Love of Paws in Fellsmere is rebuilding with more than $100,000 in community support after a March 9 fire destroyed the sanctuary and killed 11 cats. Ted Pankiewicz founded the nonprofit sanctuary in 2014 in memory of his late wife, who always wanted to start a rescue. Pankiewicz suffered burns to his arms during the fire as he tried to save the animals.

The sanctuary operates differently than traditional rescues. When pets arrive at For the Love of Paws, they stay for the rest of their lives, with the organization caring for them as their own. The sanctuary also serves vulnerable residents across the Treasure Coast by supplying 12,000 to 15,000 pounds of pet food each month to senior citizens, disabled people, and veterans struggling to feed their pets.

The new facility will be built entirely of steel and include enhanced safety features to prevent another tragedy. A security system will alert the fire department directly when smoke is detected, and an interior sprinkler system will be installed throughout the building. "The new building is going to be all steel, and we're going to be having a security system put in where the smoke detectors immediately alert the fire department, and there will be a sprinkler system inside too, which I'm sure will piss off the cats, but it's better," Pankiewicz said.

The community response to the fire deeply moved Pankiewicz and his team. "The response from the community was just as emotional as the fire was, but in the opposite. The fire made us cry tears of sorrow, and the community made us cry tears of gratitude," Pankiewicz said. The new facility is expected to be a cage-free space with an outdoor catio where cats can roam freely. The sanctuary will continue its mission of providing lifelong care for animals while supporting pet owners in need throughout the community.

cards.headline: Free and reduced-price meal applications open for Indian River County students
cards.teaser: Families in Indian River County can apply for free or reduced-price meals for students starting July 15 for the 2026-2027 school year.
cards.body:
Families in Indian River County can apply for free or reduced-price meals for students starting July 15. Students at six Indian River County schools can receive free meals during the 2026-2027 school year through federal nutrition programs. Other families in the district may still qualify for free or reduced-price meals based on household size and income criteria. Families are encouraged to complete one application per household to determine eligibility.

 To apply, families need their child's Student ID number, their child's full formal name as listed in FOCUS, a valid email address, and internet access or the LINQ Connect mobile app. Families who receive Florida Medicaid benefits need their 10-digit Medicaid case number that begins with the number 1. The case number can be found by logging into a MyACCESS account or looking at the Notice of Eligibility Review letter from the Florida Department of Children and Families.

 Families can visit www.LINQConnect.com to sign in or create an account, search for Indian River County Public Schools in Vero Beach, and add their student using the Student ID and formal name. To start the meal application, families should click School Services at the top menu and select Free and Reduced Meal Application. Families with questions can contact Shawn O'Keefe, the district's nutrition services director, at 772-564-5041 or shawn.okeefe@indianriverschools.org.

cards.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to JFK route in September, citing low demand
cards.teaser: JetBlue is ending its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport on Sept. 9, just nine months after the route launched in December.
cards.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. Dambeck said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates, with air carriers fluctuating based off of demand.

 Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time if the airline had stayed with it. Ahern said the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach is hard to beat because it is easy and close. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds.

 Dambeck said JetBlue will evaluate continuously, so just because the route is gone now does not mean it will never come back. The Boston route from Vero Beach is seeing great demand, Dambeck said.

cards.headline: Waterspouts, lightning strikes and fires batter Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County
cards.teaser: Friday's severe weather left a trail of impacts across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County, including waterspouts in Sebastian, lightning strikes and brush fires in Port St. Lucie.
cards.body:
Friday's severe weather left a trail of impacts across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. Video sent to the WPTV newsroom from Sebastian showed a large waterspout passing over the Indian River Lagoon Friday afternoon. In Port St. Lucie, WPTV weather spotters captured video of heavy rain moving through the area.

 Merry Moore O'Rourke said her rain gauge caught over 3 inches. Moore O'Rourke described the sudden change in conditions, saying it got black, the wind started raging and the sky lit up like she had not seen.

 Severe weather stretched to Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning. Port St. Lucie also saw significant lightning activity. Lucie County Fire District said crews contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that a lightning strike ignited vegetation in a nearby lot.

 At the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue, fire crews responded to an evening house fire. Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause, as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate. Moore O'Rourke said the storms were radical and a little scary.

cards.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating in September. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates based on passenger numbers.

 "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. He added that JetBlue "just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for" with the New York route.

 Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot at success. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time if given more opportunity. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked.

 I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He noted the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach, saying, "It's easy. It's close." His comments reflect concerns from local travelers who appreciated having direct access to New York without driving to larger airports in South Florida or Orlando.

 The Boston route continues to perform well at Vero Beach Regional Airport, with Dambeck saying "Boston is seeing great demand." Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time, demonstrating continued interest in that northeastern connection. The contrast between the two routes highlights how different markets can perform differently even when serving similar geographic regions. While both Boston and New York are major northeastern cities, the Boston service has attracted enough passengers to remain viable while the JFK route struggled to build a sustainable customer base.

 Dambeck said the door is not closed on the JFK route returning in the future, noting "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back." This leaves open the possibility that JetBlue could restore service to New York if conditions change or demand increases. Airlines regularly reassess their route networks based on seasonal patterns, economic conditions, and shifting travel preferences. For now, Vero Beach travelers seeking to reach New York will need to connect through other cities or use alternative airports.

cards.headline: JetBlue ending direct flights from Vero Beach to JFK Airport in September
cards.teaser: JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December.
cards.body:
JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December. The airline announced that service between the two airports will end Sept. 9, just nine months after the route began operating with much fanfare and optimistic passengers. JetBlue said in a statement that demand for this new route has not materialized as the airline had hoped. JetBlue will continue serving Vero Beach through its Boston route and has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service.

 All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information. The JFK-Vero Beach route was seen as a major win for the Treasure Coast when it launched in December 2025, providing direct access to one of the nation's busiest airports and potentially boosting tourism to the area. The inaugural flight brought enthusiastic passengers who called the service a game changer for connecting family and friends between New York and the Treasure Coast.

 The route's cancellation comes as a disappointment to local officials and residents who had hoped the direct connection would strengthen ties between the two regions. The discontinuation of the JFK route after such a short period highlights the challenges smaller regional airports face in sustaining air service to major hubs. While JetBlue's Boston service will continue to provide some connectivity for Vero Beach travelers, the loss of direct access to JFK eliminates what many saw as a crucial link to the New York metropolitan area. The airline has not indicated whether it might reconsider the route in the future or explore other destinations from Vero Beach Regional Airport.

 The route had been viewed as important infrastructure for the region when it first began operations, with hopes that convenient access to JFK would help strengthen economic and personal connections between the Treasure Coast and the New York metropolitan area. The short lifespan of the route underscores the difficulties regional airports encounter when trying to establish and maintain service to major transportation hubs.
